audience: Finance users who need to see how overdue one customer's balance is, for example before a credit review or a collections call.
goal: Produce an **Accounts Receivable Ageing** report for a **single customer**: open **Reporting › Aged Receivable**, filter **Partners** to the customer, read the balance across every ageing duration (**At Date, 1-30, 31-60, 61-90, 91-120, Older, Total**), unfold the customer line to see the entries behind it, and export the report to **PDF** or **XLSX**.
before: You can open the **Accounting** app and its **Reporting** menu.
You know the customer's name (the guide uses **DIDULA POWER ELECTRICLES (PVT) LIMITED**).
Decide the cut-off date. The guide leaves it on **today**, so every open item up to today is included.
outcome: The report shows **only the chosen customer**, with the balance split across the ageing columns.
You have unfolded the customer line and can see each open invoice or credit note in its own ageing column.
You know where to export the report as a PDF or a spreadsheet.
notes: The screenshots were captured by an automated run on a **test database**. The customer's entries and amounts are test data and will differ from your live figures. In this data all three entries are dated 01/07/2025, so they all fall in the **Older** column and add up to −1.00.
The red banner at the top of the screenshots ("Database neutralized for testing") only appears on test databases.
The automated run only checks that the **PDF** and **XLSX** buttons are present — it does not download a file.

phases.title: Open the Aged Receivable report
phases.summary: Go from the Accounting app to the ageing report.
phases.checkpoint: The **Aged Receivable** report is open, with its filter buttons and the **PDF** / **XLSX** buttons visible.

phases.title: Choose the cut-off date and the customer
phases.summary: Check the report date, then narrow the report to one customer.
phases.checkpoint: The report shows **only your chosen customer**, as of the date you want.

phases.title: Read and export the ageing
phases.summary: Unfold the customer, read the ageing columns, and export the report.
phases.checkpoint: You have read the customer's balance across the ageing columns and know where to export it.

glossary.meaning: A report that groups what customers owe you by **how overdue** it is, so you can see which balances are old.
The cut-off date of the report. Items are aged as at this date.
Amounts that are **not yet due** on the report date.
Amounts that are that many **days overdue**.
The sum of all the columns for the row.
A negative figure means the customer has paid, or been credited, **more** than they were invoiced — you owe them rather than the other way round.
The customer (or vendor) a journal entry belongs to.

1.title: Open the Accounting app
1.do: On the Odoo home screen, click the **Accounting** app.
actions: Go to the Odoo home screen (the grid of app icons).
Find the **Accounting** icon.
Click it.
1.see: The Accounting app opens with its menu bar across the top (Dashboard, Customers, Vendors, Accounting, Reporting …).
1.tip: You are about to produce an Accounts Receivable Ageing report for one customer.
1.why: Every accounting report lives inside the Accounting app, so this is always the starting point.

2.title: Open the Reporting menu
2.do: In the top menu bar, click **Reporting**.
actions: Look at the menu bar across the top.
Click **Reporting**.
2.see: A drop-down listing all the Accounting reports, including the ageing reports.
2.tip: If the **Reporting** entry is missing, widen the browser window — the last menu entries hide behind a **+** when the window is narrow.
2.why: The Reporting menu groups all financial reports. The ageing reports sit under Partner Reports.

3.title: Open Aged Receivable
3.do: In the **Partner Reports** group, click **Aged Receivable**.
3.where: Accounting app > Reporting > Partner Reports > Aged Receivable
actions: With the Reporting menu open, find the **Partner Reports** group.
Click **Aged Receivable**.
Wait for the report to load.
3.see: The **Aged Receivable** report, with filter buttons across the top (**As of** date, **Account: Receivable**, **Partners**, **Options**) and the **PDF** and **XLSX** buttons at the top left.
3.tip: This report buckets every outstanding customer balance by how overdue it is.
3.why: Aged Receivable lists what customers still owe, split by how long the amount has been overdue. Use it for credit reviews and collection calls.

4.title: Check the report date
4.do: Look at the **As of** date button at the top. Leave it on **today**.
4.where: Aged Receivable report > As of date button
actions: Find the **As of …** button at the top of the report.
Read the date.
Leave it as it is (today) unless you need an earlier cut-off.
4.see: The button shows today's date, so every ageing duration up to today is included.
4.tip: The **As of** date is the cut-off for the whole report. Change it only if you need the ageing as it was on an earlier date — for example at month end.
4.why: Ageing is always measured at a single date. Items are placed in a column according to how many days they are overdue on that date, so changing it changes the buckets.

5.title: Open the Partners filter
5.do: Click the **Partners** button at the top of the report.
actions: Find the **Partners** button in the row of filters.
Click it.
A box opens where you can search for customers.
5.see: A drop-down with a search box for partners.
5.tip: Leaving Partners empty would show every customer — use this filter to narrow the report to one.
5.why: By default the report lists every customer. Filtering by partner narrows it to the one customer you are interested in.

6.title: Search for the customer
6.do: Type the customer's name in the **Partners** search box.
6.where: Aged Receivable report > Partners > search box
actions: Click the search box inside the Partners drop-down.
Type **Didula power**.
Wait for the matching customers to appear.
6.see: A list of customers that match what you typed.
6.tip: Part of the name is enough — you do not need to type it in full.
6.why: The search matches any part of the customer name, so a short fragment is enough. Typing does not filter the report yet; you must pick a result in the next step.

7.title: Choose the customer
7.do: In the list, click **DIDULA POWER ELECTRICLES (PVT) LIMITED**.
7.where: Aged Receivable report > Partners > search results
actions: Find **DIDULA POWER ELECTRICLES (PVT) LIMITED** in the list of matches.
Click it.
Wait a moment — the report reloads.
7.see: The report now shows **only this customer**, and the customer's name appears as a line under the **Aged Receivable** total.
7.warning: Check the name before you click. Several customers can have similar names, and picking the wrong one gives you somebody else's figures.
7.why: Picking the customer applies the filter and reloads the report. Check the report shows exactly one customer line before continuing.

8.title: Unfold the customer line
8.do: Click the customer's name to **unfold** it.
actions: Find the customer's name in the report (in bold, with **Open** and **Journal Items** buttons next to it).
Click the name.
The line unfolds and the filter panel closes.
8.see: Under the customer's line, **every open invoice and credit note** behind the balance, each one in its own ageing column.
8.tip: Use **Open** to go to the customer, or **Journal Items** to see the accounting lines in full.
8.why: The customer line only shows totals. Unfolding it lists each open invoice or credit note so you can see which items make up each ageing column.

9.title: Read the ageing columns
9.do: Read **across the row** to see how old the customer's balance is.
actions: Look at the column headings above the figures.
Read them from left to right: **At Date, 1-30, 31-60, 61-90, 91-120, Older, Total**.
Find which column each of the customer's amounts sits in.
9.see: Every ageing duration is shown. No extra setting is needed — the report always includes all of them.
9.tip: A negative **Total** is a credit balance: the customer has paid or been credited more than was invoiced.
9.why: The columns run from not yet due (At Date) to more than 120 days overdue (Older). A balance sitting far to the right is the most overdue and the most urgent to collect.

10.title: Export the report
10.do: To keep a copy, click **PDF** or **XLSX** at the top left of the report.
actions: Look at the buttons at the top-left of the report.
Click **PDF** to print or email the report.
Or click **XLSX** to download it as a spreadsheet.
10.see: A file download. The export keeps the customer filter and all the ageing columns exactly as shown on screen.
10.tip: That completes the tour: open the report, filter to one customer, read the ageing, and export it.
10.why: Exporting keeps the filter and columns you see on screen, so the file matches what you reviewed. Use PDF for sharing and XLSX for further analysis.
